en: The Essential Method for Recitation of the Dhāraṇī of the Supreme, Peerless,
and Greatly Majestic Vajra Unobstructed Great Maṇḍala of the White Parasol Great Uṣṇīṣa Rāja.
I take refuge in all the Tathāgatas throughout the entire realm of phenomena,
The wondrously manifested forms of the Honored Ones in every atom and land. I pay homage to the most supreme Buddha-uṣṇīṣa family,
And to the Great Compassionate One and the assembly of Lotus-holding Bodhisattvas.
Purifying the stains of karmic obstructions and extensively benefiting all sentient beings,
we take refuge in the Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi, the King of the Treasury.
Having received from the Buddha this firm [teaching], he protects and sustains all.
The assembly of the luminous Honored Ones and Great Sages, the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas,
and the hosts of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas,
constantly pay homage day and night to this Great White Parasol, which universally covers the great trichiliocosm.
His spiritual transformations are inconceivable; Like space, he is without obstruction.
All Buddhas praise him, Calling him the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa King;
By this he realized Bodhi, And is able to turn the unsurpassed Dharma.
The multitude of sages have traveled and studied together; I too shall practice in accordance with them.
I briefly extract the essential ritual procedures; may you all deign to grant your protection.
First, with *HŪṂ*, enter the maṇḍala and behold all the Buddhas.
First, purify the three karmas; awaken to the stainless body of one's own nature, wherein the vessel of the body is entirely pure.
Realizing that one’s essence is identical to all Tathāgatas and pervades all of space, direct the mind to pay universal homage.
I repent of boundless transgressions, Which together return to the emptiness of the Dharma-nature.
I entreat all Tathāgatas To remain forever in the world without passing away.
I rejoice in the merit of humans and devas, Which extensively benefits all living beings.
Dedicating with a single mind, may we together ascend to *sarvajñā* (omniscience).
I make this vow for this life and all future ones: may I always be able to extensively practice the bodhisattva path and purify the vessel-world (*bhājanaloka*). The mantra is as follows:
Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | Oṃ jvālānuśobhanāya svāhā | This is the Great Pure Illumination Mantra.
This applies universally to the Tathāgata family.
First, perform the ritual sprinkling and purification,
and then seal off the recitation chamber.
Having recited it seven times,
the three karmas of body, speech,
and mind will extend throughout the entire dharma realm.
All are entirely pure.
Next, one should universally prostrate to all Tathāgatas.
The mantra is as follows:
Recite the mantra "Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāmeghasamudraspharaṇa" three times, while directing the mind to be identical with the *dharmadhātu*.
Pervading as many lands as there are atoms,
one’s acts of worship are entirely perfected.
Next, the mantra for repenting of karmic obstacles from beginningless time is as follows:
Oṃ sarvapāpaharaṇa vajrāya svāhā. Recite this mantra three times to repent for all transgressions.
"Anānantarya sins are like grass;
they are incinerated and utterly extinguished without remainder.

At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the great assembly of all bodhisattvas: "O sons of noble family, you should bestow the mantra-body of the incomparable power of the samādhi 'Birth of All Tathāgatas,' which surpasses all [other] Tathāgatas, as well as the true great mudrās and mantras of the families of all Tathāgatas."
Possessing peerless majestic light and supernormal powers,
arising from boundless, extraordinary, and great spiritual majesty,
he is able to give birth to all bodhisattvas.
It can destroy all hosts of Māras who cause depression,
subdue all those who are difficult to tame, and,
by giving rise to a mind of loving-kindness, accomplish all activities and bring about every benefit and success.
Now, the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) will be explained.
Next, facing the deity, sit in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka).
Anoint your hands with fragrant unguents and form the samaya-mudrās of all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the Vajra family.
Insert the hands into the *kṣepaṇa* mudrā with the thumbs and wisdom fingers extended together;
while reciting the mantra according to the verse,
place the seal upon the crown of the head.
This is the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) of the heart of all Tathāgatas.
Next, bend the wisdom finger (jñānāṅgulī) into the palm;
this is the secret seal (guhyamudrā) for holding the lotus.
Recite the mantra following the phrases,
then move it to rest upon the right side of the crown.
Next, bend the *dhyāna* (left) hand and place it within the palm.
Next, one should extend the *vajra-pāṇi* [gesture] of the Wisdom Perfection;
this is the secret mudrā held by all the Vajra families.
While reciting the mantra syllables,
move the mudrā and place it upon the left side of the head;
all are identical with the vidyā.
The three families are all fully present.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ*. *Āḥ vīra hūṃ khaṃ*. This binds the great mudrās of all Tathāgatas and others.
By means of the mantra of Great Diligent Valor and the empowerment of the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas,
one is able to completely liberate [beings] from the hells, the animal realm, and the evil destiny of Yama.
It enables all sentient beings to perform the deeds of a Tathāgata;
it summons the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas and noble ones,
and can invoke the various devas, including Brahmā, Śakra, Yama, Varuṇa, and Kuvera.
If even a Bodhisattva of the tenth stage, who possesses great mastery,
is able to summon [the deities], how much more so others?
Next, perform the mudrā for binding the vajra armor to protect the body.
Form the hook-fist with both hands;
the left is held horizontally and facing upward below the navel,
while the right hooks and presses down upon the five locations.
At the heart, forehead, shoulders, throat, and crown, recite the mantra as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām oṃ bhujaṅgavajra-teja hūṃ*. By means of this armor-mantra (*kavaca-vidyā*), [one is protected].
The practitioner should apply [the mudrā] and seal the entire body; thus,
great protection is accomplished.
Among all the Buddha-uṣṇīṣas,
this mudrā possesses great majestic power;
no māras can assail or oppress it.
Donning the armor like a king,
one can accomplish all tasks and swiftly attain siddhi.
Next, one should perform the Great Wheel Seal (Mahācakra-mudrā) and the Vajra Wheel.
Next, one should bind the Great Seal of Aparājita.
This is the mudrā for the Vidyārāja to dispel demonic obstacles.
One should kneel with the right knee and extend the left knee;
the left hand is turned backward in a gesturing motion.
With the right fist held upright and extended before the heart,
advance toward the opponent with a posture of intent to strike.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ hulu hulu caṇḍāli maṇḍaki svāhā | This is the Great Mantra of Aparājita.
This is what the Buddha has taught:
it can destroy all Māras and can dispel all obstacles.
The Great Powerful One, Lord of Desire;
the King of the World’s Māra Armies;
even Pāpīyān is sovereign.
O World-Protector of Great Majestic Power,
you who subdue immeasurable *kūṭadha* māras—
if they should wish to create obstacles and difficulties, [may they be subdued].
They manifest various forms,
the terrifying shapes of Māra’s armies;
this occurs through the binding of mudrās and the recitation of mantras.
Therefore, they will all naturally retreat and disperse.
One should perform this empowerment when seeking to accomplish the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
In places of great obstacles,
one will always receive great protection.
Next, perform the mudrā for invitation.
Cross the two hands at the inner palms with the fists clenched;
extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers upward and join them,
bending their upper joints into hooks.
The coming and going constitute the invitation.
To universally invite all the Buddhas and Uṣṇīṣarājas, the mantra is as follows.
Having formed the mudrā:
First, place incense and flowers upon the mudrā and cast them into the maṇḍala while reciting the mantra:

*Namo bhagavato uṣṇīṣāya | ehe hi bhagavan dharma-rāja-praticchanna-māraga jambu-svapna-dvīpa-maline | jhaḥ phaṭ rākṣasa-pratihata-māra-parakrama svāhā.* Bind the mudrā and recite the vidyā three times.
Awakening all Buddhas and inviting all Tathāgatas,
may they all descend and arrive.
Next, bind the Light-Cluster Mudrā:
extend both the *dāna* (thumb) and *maitrī* (forefinger) straight upward;
bend the *śīla* (middle finger) at its head joint and place it upon [the thumb], and join the *kṣānti* (ring finger) and *praṇidhāna* (pinky) together in reverse.
The *dhyāna* and *prajñā* [fingers] are extended side-by-side and straight;
the *vīrya* [finger] is bent and placed against them to press down on the heads of the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* [fingers].
Rotate [the hands] to form the boundary (*sīmābandha*).
Recite the mantra seven times:

*Namo samantabuddhānām, apratihataśāsanānām. Oṃ tathāgatadhvajānavalo-kitamūrdhan devara siṃha huṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka vidhaka vidhaka nara nara vidhara vidhara khana khana bhinna bhinna hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. If used for protecting the body:
This is the mudrā of the three-pronged vajra.
When invoking the deity, one uses the vajra mudrā;
by making the two index fingers into hooks and moving them back and forth, this is precisely how one summons [the deity].
This Great Uṣṇīṣa King is named the Mass of Radiance;
its fierce flames blaze and spread abroad.
Like the blazing conflagration at the end of an eon,
its power is inconceivable;
it can utterly destroy all things.
The hosts of celestial Māras and non-Buddhist paths, Maheśvara,
and the mighty Nārāyaṇa.
Together with all other classes of devas,
all their various supernormal powers were extinguished and utterly destroyed, leaving nothing behind.
The Great Bodhisattvas who uphold the vidyā-mantras, such as Hayagrīva and others,
having heard the recitation of this mantra.
With a majestic radiance like a gathered point,
it resides upon the crown of the Great Buddha’s head,
extinguishing all calamities.
Within an area of twelve *yojanas*, one establishes a great boundary (*sīmā*). Next, one performs the mudrā for accomplishing the rite:
with both hands, form fists by interlocking the thumbs inside.
By extending, contracting, and joining the hands in the gesture of endurance and aspiration, one can accomplish all things;
by circling them three times counter-clockwise, it is perfected.
The mantra for expelling obstacles is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ, cāru hūṃ bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the mantra for accomplishing activities.
The Heart of All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣas:
by the mere act of recollecting it,
all obstacles on land and water [are removed].
All those who wish to cause harm shall have their mouths bound;
one should form the mudrā at the heart.
Empower the five locations.
Next, form the lotus mudrā,
like an eight-petaled lotus in full bloom.
I reverently offer this seat to all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas with a sincere heart.
Recite the mantra seven times.
Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām | Oṃ hūṃ kāmala-ya svāhā | By means of this offering.
The Buddhas shall accept this seat;
in the future, one will surely attain the supreme and wondrous Vajrāsana.
Next, perform the offering of argha.
This vast and authentic offering generally consists of fragrant white flowers.
Offer with a sincere heart.
Then, using the vajra-fist,
join the tips of the thumbs and ring fingers together.
Bend the *jinyoku* (vīrya) behind the back;
join the *zenchi* (dhyāna-prajñā) at the base of the *jinken* (vīryendriya).
The mantra is as follows:
Namo bhagavate śrīye maṃ khaṃ taṃ saṃ puṣpaṃ duṃ maṃ niḥ pañca pratisamaye hira hira sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhite dharmarāje pratihata ya svāhā. By reciting this mantra:
In order to make offerings to the Tathāgata,
they pervade all lands as numerous as atoms,
accomplishing every kind of exquisite offering.
Next, bind the Buddha-eye mudrā.
Among all the Buddha-uṣṇīṣas,
one should employ this great mudrā.
Purely receive and uphold it;
it is the most supreme for extinguishing all sins.
Regarding the King of the Buddhas' Uṣṇīṣas:
Always bind this mudrā;
you will certainly attain siddhi and will surely achieve accomplishment before long.
Regarding all the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa dharmas,
even if one were to accumulate merit for a hundred kalpas,
if one obtains this seal and mantra, [the goal is attained].
Its merit is equal to theirs.
This mantra of the Buddha-Eye is capable of accomplishing all activities.
This vidyā was received and upheld by the Tathāgatas from ten koṭis of Buddhas;
it is realized simply by recollecting it.
All the noble deities will manifest;
all the teachings of mantra shall be accomplished.
Before those who are violent, wicked, and wrathful,
one should recite this to win their joy;
even the unruly and evil spirits [will be subdued].
All who are subdued will follow in harmony;
in places of battle and litigation,
all shall attain peaceful purification.
Recite this seven times, both before and after [the main mantra],
and you will swiftly attain realization and signs of efficacy.
Next, bind the seal of the One-Syllable King of the Golden Wheel Uṣṇīṣa.
Cross the two hands at the inner palms with the fists clenched;
extend both the *kṣānti* (middle) and *praṇidhi* (ring) fingers together, joining them,
and bend the third phalanx of the upper joints.
Bend the head of the power of progress;
extend the meditative concentration and wisdom equally.
The sevenfold mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ jvala oṃ [as many as the sands of the Ganges].
That which was spoken by the Tathāgatas,
that which the present Buddhas now speak,
and that which the future Buddhas shall speak.
This mudrā is named the Great Mudrā;
it is taught as the Cakravartin of the Uṣṇīṣa.
This mudrā is itself the Buddha.
Benefiting all sentient beings,
through the great majesty of vidyā,
one subdues all the noble ones and sages.
Within a radius of fifty *yojanas*,
it prevents other honored ones and the Bodhisattvas of the ten stages from descending.
They are bewildered and lose their original minds;
how much less could others of lesser kind manifest supernatural powers?
The wise one accomplishes this for people.
If at this place where the seal is bound,
there are various evil māras and obstacles on the ground.
One would not dare to dwell in such a place for even a hundred koṭis of kalpas,
nor even for as many as the sands of a thousand Ganges Rivers.
Even with grains of sand as numerous as these,
one could not fully describe their merits and benefits.
Praising the power of his majestic virtue,
if a wise person receives and upholds it,
they will never be thwarted or destroyed.
The Great Teacher, the Tathāgata,
has taught that one cannot sufficiently praise those who practice the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
One will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, bind the general seal for the accomplishment of all Uṣṇīṣas:
cross the two hands at the palms with the fists clenched.
Extend the ring finger and the little finger upward;
bend the upper joints of these two fingers.
This is universally applicable for all uses.
Recite the mantra seven times.
Seal it upon the crown of the head and then release it. *Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ nṛ-maṇḍa svāhā*. By means of this seal:
Just as when one beholds the Buddhas being invited,
the various yakṣas, nāgas, and asura hosts who are difficult to subdue [are likewise summoned].
All evil rākṣasas, as well as all māras, [are subdued] by the majestic power of this vidyā.
All terrors are completely dissolved.
If one attains this mudrā,
one will be able to obtain all forms of peace and happiness.
The king and those equal to him in the world constantly benefit them;
those who seek the benefits of the Dharma [should likewise act].
One will certainly obtain [it] through the accomplishment of the fruit of the Universal King of Mantras.

Next, bind the Great Seal of the White Parasol Uṣṇīṣa King, which universally covers the trichiliocosm so that its boundaries cannot be seen; or alternatively, bind the Single-Minded Seal of the ten billion Buddhas.
Recite the Great Mantra seven times.
Next, perform the root mudrā of Sitātapatrā.
Join the two hands with palms hollowed and open;
bend the fingers of the *śīla* hand and insert them into the palm,
facing them toward the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* [thumbs].
Simultaneously press the fingers against the back of the hand;
advance the force and bend them into a circle.
This is the Buddha’s Parasol Mudrā.
Recite the mantra seven times and then scatter it over the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām | Oṃ tathāgatoṣṇīṣānavalokitamūrdha-kīla-vare | Oṃ mama hūṃ ṭiṭṭi | This is the Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa King.
Supreme and without equal,
this is the power of the Buddha’s great compassion,
flowing forth as a lion’s roar.
Empowered by all Buddhas,
the Great Compassion illuminates the darkness of sorrow;
profoundly deep, it is utterly stainless.
It causes all manner of auspiciousness to arise;
neither bodhisattvas nor devas can obstruct or destroy it.
They shall attain non-retrogression;
all shall be at peace and secure,
and no poisons shall be able to harm them.
The devas and nāgas dare not approach it.
By copying it out and reciting and upholding it,
one will swiftly realize siddhi.
Next, take up the rosary,
empower it seven times,
and hold it upon the crown of your head.
Nevertheless, having performed the recitation one hundred and eight or one thousand and eight times,
collect the beads and place them back in their original location.
Again, bind the mudrā of the Honored One, abide in samādhi,
and praise the virtues of the Buddha.
Make offerings as previously presented.
Then, bind the samaya mudrā to protect the body, prostrate to the Buddha, and withdraw.
Form the bead-holding mudrā.
With the left and right hands, using the dhyāna and jñāna fingers respectively,
pinch the fingernails of the fingers of the "precept" direction.
Extend the fingers of the patience and vow mudrās and extend the fingers of the diligence power mudrā;
bend them behind the patience and vow mudrās,
hold the beads, and perform the recitation.
If one wishes to abide in the deportment of a Buddha,
one should assume the heroic posture,
sitting upright with legs crossed in the full lotus position.
Form the Buddha-kṛti mudrā:
with the left hand, palm facing upward, placed upon the lap;
with the right hand, the palm is held upright and turned outward.
Fasten the armor of the precepts with dhyāna;
bend the back of patience with diligence.
Recite the mantra seven times.
Then, enter into samādhi. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vīrye mahāśakti-nudari hūṃ phaṭ | vīryeṇi hūṃ phaṭ | maṅgali hūṃ phaṭ | svāhā*. If one binds this mudrā:
Without robbing them of their majestic power in this life and in future lives,
they shall attain the powers of a Tathāgata.
If one recites this mantra,
all Buddhas will grant their protection;
thus one practices the Uṣṇīṣarāja.
By constantly recollecting this at the three times of day,
one will swiftly attain accomplishment and remain unimpeded within the three realms.
This is the Great Buddha-uṣṇīṣa King;
the methods of its secret mudrās are immeasurable.
Now, for the sake of practitioners, [I shall explain them].
This is a brief collection of essential secrets.
Those who delight in the Great Dharma should seek empowerment from a master.
Having received the samaya,
one should extensively consult and study the recitation method of the Great White Parasol Great Uṣṇīṣa.
This dharma is secret;
those who have not received initiation must not hear it recklessly.
The practitioner thereby attains accomplishment.
If one intends to seek siddhi for oneself while also serving as a root master,
one must by no means transmit the secret mudrā to others;
the great samaya must be strictly maintained.
The mantra is: Oṃ śaṅkara-mahā-samayasambhava sambhava svāhā. The mantra for consecrating the rosary is:
*Namo bhagavate suteja-sattvāya svāhā.* (Recite this mantra for purifying the rosary while joining the palms and holding the beads.)
Vajra-ratna-dharma-saṃbhava-anupama-smṛti (The Peerless Mindfulness of the Arising of the Vajra-Jewel-Dharma)
